text: I'll look at the workspace to find the tax calculation code.
The bug is in `library/tax.py` at line 20, which uses `ROUND_DOWN`. Let me read the file to confirm.
The tax is quantized with `ROUND_DOWN`, which truncates half-cent amounts (e.g. 0.7250 → 0.72). The test expects round-half-up. I'll switch to `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
All 29 tests pass, including the half-cent rounding test.

args.summary: The CA sales tax (and all state taxes) was quantized in library/tax.py::calculate_tax using ROUND_DOWN, so any amount landing exactly on or above a half-cent boundary was truncated instead of rounded. For example, $10.00 * 7.25% = $0.7250 was charged as $0.72 instead of $0.73. I changed the rounding mode to ROUND_HALF_UP (updating the import accordingly). The full test suite now passes (29/29), including tests/test_tax.py::test_calculate_tax_rounds_half_up_to_the_cent.
